content.value_statement: Annotated biological matrices are complex to build, combine, and store efficiently. This skill provides practical AnnData patterns for reliable Python workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates AnnData objects from matrices and indexed observation or variable metadata.
Explains reading and writing h5ad, Zarr, CSV, Loom, 10X HDF5, and matrix formats.
Guides subsetting, filtering, transposition, copying, metadata updates, and sparse matrix conversion.
Combines datasets across observations or variables with join, merge, label, and key strategies.
Recommends backed mode, lazy access, chunking, compression, and scverse integration for larger workflows.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples but does not execute analysis or inspect datasets automatically.
It does not validate biological assumptions, experimental design, or quality-control thresholds.
Remote access examples use placeholders and require trusted URLs plus appropriate local security controls.
Package behavior can vary by installed AnnData, Scanpy, and scverse versions.

use_cases.title: Build a single-cell data object
use_cases.description: Organize count matrices, cell annotations, and gene metadata into a correctly indexed AnnData object.

use_cases.title: Combine experimental batches
use_cases.description: Merge multiple h5ad datasets while preserving batch labels and selecting appropriate join and merge strategies.

use_cases.title: Optimize large dataset storage
use_cases.description: Choose backed mode, sparse matrices, compression, Zarr chunks, or lazy access for limited-memory workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create an AnnData object
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to create an AnnData object from my matrix, cell metadata, and gene metadata. Explain required index alignment.

prompt_templates.title: Read and inspect h5ad
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me read [file.h5ad], inspect its dimensions and annotations, and choose memory-safe access for a [size] dataset.

prompt_templates.title: Concatenate study batches
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an AnnData concatenation workflow for [batch files]. Preserve source labels, compare join options, and flag metadata alignment risks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a scalable pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose a memory-efficient AnnData pipeline for [dataset description]. Cover sparse storage, backed or lazy access, chunking, validation, and reproducible outputs.

output_examples.input: How should I load a 100 GB h5ad file for metadata filtering?
output_examples.output: Open the file in read-only backed mode, filter observations through metadata, then load only the required subset into memory.

output_examples.input: How can I combine three batches without losing their origin?
output: Add a batch label with one key per source.
Choose inner or outer joins based on gene coverage.

output_examples.input: My cell metadata appears in the wrong rows after assignment.
output_examples.output: Index the external table by cell identifier, align it to observation names, verify missing values, then assign the aligned column.

best_practices: Keep observation and variable indices unique, stable, and aligned before assignment or concatenation.
Use sparse matrices, categoricals, backed mode, or lazy access when dataset size exceeds available memory.
Preserve raw measurements and record processing parameters before filtering or transformation.
anti_patterns: Do not densify sparse matrices without estimating the resulting memory requirement.
Do not assign metadata by row position when identifiers can provide explicit alignment.
Do not use outer concatenation without reviewing missing variables and fill behavior.

faq.question: What data does AnnData store?
faq.answer: AnnData stores a primary matrix with observation metadata, variable metadata, layers, embeddings, pairwise annotations, unstructured values, and optional raw data.

faq.question: Which file format should I choose?
faq.answer: Use h5ad for common local workflows. Consider Zarr for cloud storage, parallel access, or workflows that benefit from configurable chunks.

faq.question: Can this skill handle datasets larger than memory?
faq.answer: It explains backed mode, lazy reads, sparse storage, chunking, and selective loading. Actual feasibility depends on operations, formats, and available resources.

faq.question: Does this skill perform single-cell analysis?
faq.answer: It provides AnnData and Scanpy workflow guidance. It does not execute analysis or replace biological validation.

faq.question: How should I combine multiple batches?
faq.answer: Concatenate observations, preserve a source label, select inner or outer joins deliberately, and verify index and metadata consistency.

faq.question: Can it access remote datasets?
faq.answer: It documents remote Zarr access and URL downloads. Use trusted sources, verify downloaded data, and follow local network policies.
